title: How DC Cut Sewage Overflows by 90% With One Tunnel #shorts
summary: DC Water's Anacostia River Tunnel, 23 feet wide, holds up to 100 million gallons of combined sewage in heavy rain and sends it to the Blue Plains plant. Since 2018, overflows into the Anacostia are down 90%.
sources: Since the Anacostia River Tunnel was completed in March 2018, combined sewer overflows to the Anacostia River have been reduced by 90 percent; the tunnel delivers captured overflows to the Blue Plains plant, where they are treated before discharge to the Potomac (DC Water, Anacostia River Tunnel Project): https://www.dcwater.com/projects/anacostia-river-tunnel-project

The tunnel has a 23-foot inside diameter and can capture and hold up to 100 million gallons of combined sewage in heavy rainfalls (DC Water news release, 28 Mar 2018): https://www.dcwater.com/whats-going-on/news/dc-water-delivers-cleaner-anacostia-river-opening-first-leg-massive-tunnel

Blue Plains treats close to 300 million gallons of wastewater a day (daily capacity 384 million gallons) and is the largest plant of its kind in the world (DC Water, Blue Plains Advanced Wastewater Treatment Plant): https://www.dcwater.com/about-dc-water/what-we-do/wastewater-treatment/blue-plains

In a combined sewer system, wastewater and stormwater flow through the same pipes; in wet weather the combined flow can overwhelm the system, and permitted outfalls act as relief points that discharge untreated or partially treated stormwater and wastewater into nearby waterbodies (US EPA, Combined Sewer Overflow Basics): https://epa.gov/npdes/combined-sewer-overflow-basics
